Republic Of the DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT Center. EDSA corner Quezon Aventn West Triangle, Quezon City http: ltwww. dilg.gov.ph 28 FEB DILG OPINION No. DIR HERMINIGILDA G. GARSULA Acting Regional Director Bureau of Local Government Finance — Region X Department of Finance Zone 6, Tejero St., Cagayan de Oro Misamis Oriental Dear Dir. Garsula: This pertains to your letters dated 29 June 2018 and 19 July 2018 requesting guidance from this Department on the following issues which we quote hereunder, respectively, to wit: 1. Should there be any formality/process of the office of the Department of the Interior and Local Government for the installation of the legitimate Municipal Mayor of Pantar, Lanao del Norte, before this office can act on the request of the Local Chief Executive in relation to the provisions of Section 46 of the Local Government Code of 1991, specifically upon the lapse of the thirty (30) day period? 2. Whether the Acting Municipal Mayor of Pantar, Lanao del Norte, shall by operation of law be allowed to issue a recommendation for the relief; recall and designation ofa municipal treasurer after the lapse of thirty (30) days as provided for under Section 46 of the Local Government. The above-quoted queries were posted for purposes of acting on the request of Acting Mayor Hadji Rakim Umpara Alingan of Pantar, Lanao del Norte to issue a Regional Special Personnel Order to appoint Rocma M. Ampang as Municipal Treasurer of Pantar and to revoke the designation of Noraima Hadji Serad Racman made by Mayor Jabar D. Tago as in charge of the office (ICO) or officer-in-charge (OIC), Municipal Treasurer and whether the Acting Municipal Mayor of Pantar, Lanao del Norte, shall by operation of law, be allowed to issue recommendation for the relief, recall and designation of a municipal treasurer after the lapse of thirty (30) days as provided for under Section 46 of the Local Government Code, respectively. At the outset, it bears stressing that fugitive from justice includes not only those who flee after conviction to avoid punishment but likewise those who, after being charged,

flee to avoid prosecutionL. Considering that Mayor Tago is a fugitive from justice coupled with other circumstances (e.g. his physical absence in the Office of the Mayor and his non- performance of duties as local chief executive) already amounts to a temporary incapacity to perform his duties and functions2. Hence, there arises temporary vacancy in the office of the municipal mayor. Following the rule on automatic succession provided in Section 46 of the Local Government Code (LGC), since the Municipal Mayor is temporarily incapacitated to perform his duties for physical or legal reasons, the Municipal Vice-Mayor shall automatically exercise the powers and perform the duties and functions of the local chief executive concerned, except the power to appoint, suspend, or dismiss employees which can only be exercised if the period of temporary incapacity exceeds thirty (30) working days. Assuming that Mayor Tago's temporary incapacity already exceeded the 30 working-day period, then Acting Mayor Alingan can now exercise the power to appoint or dismiss employees. However, Section 470 of the LGC and Article 122(b)(1) of its Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) provides that, municipal treasurer shall be appointed by the Secretary of Finance from a list of at least three (3) ranking, eligible recommendees of the mayor, subject to civil service law, rules and regulations. It is clear from the said provision that it is the Secretary of Finance that has the power to appoint treasurers. It is within the Secretary of Finance's power to terminate the said designation, as well as to appoint a permanent municipal treasurer, provided that the necessary qualifications and appropriate eligibility are met, in accordance with the provisions of law, rules and standards promulgated in pursuance thereof (Section 9(a) of CSC MC. No. 24, S.2017)3. Hence, this Department answers affrmatively with respect to your query on whether the Acting Municipal Mayor of Pantar, Lanao del Norte, shall by operation of law, be allowed to issue recommendation for the relief, recall and designation of a municipal treasurer after the lapse of thirty (30) days, pursuant to Section 470 of the LGC and Article of its IRR. The Acting Mayor's power over the said municipal treasurer is merely supervisory pursuant to Section 444(b)(x) Of the LGC, to wit: "Ensure that all executive officials and employees ofthe municipality faithfully discharge their duties and functions asprovided bylaw and this Code, and cause to be instituted administrative or judicial Rodriguez vs. COMELEC etal., G.R. No. 112889, 18 April 1995 2 DILG Legal Opinion No. 03, S. 2016, 21 January 2016 3 Sec. 9. Employment Status. The employment status in the civil service shall be determined by the appointment issued, which can be any of the following: a. Permanent —an appointment issued to a person who meets all the qualification requirements of the position to which he/she is being appointed to, including the appropriate eligibility, in accordance with the provisions of law, rules and standards promulgated in pursuance thereof

proceedings against any official or employee of the municipality who may have committed an offense in the performance of his official duties. " Lastly, we are of the considered view that this Department's participation is limited to the issuance of the Certification recognizing Vice-Mayor Alingan as the Acting Mayor of Pantar, Lanao del Norte, which is not even a condition sine qua non before appointing a municipal treasurer by the Secretary of Finance. Thank you. Very truly yours, By Authority of the Secretary: C. SACENDONCILLO, CESO 111 Undersecretary CC: Dir. Arnel M. Agabe Regional Director DILG-Region X (Northern Mindanao) Hon. Hadji Rakim Umpara Alingan Acting Municipal Mayor Municipality of Pantar Province of Lanao del Norte Ls,90B/
